purpose: Local semantic guidance for multimodal supervision, OCR reconciliation, translation grouping, and placement planning.
instance_rules: Translate every spatially distinct visible instance unless the supervisor explicitly links it to one shared local translation.
Equipment identifiers and drawing codes remain literal, but their surrounding functional descriptions still require translation.
Do not treat dimensions, grid labels, levels, scale values, phone numbers, email addresses, URLs, or company registration numbers as untranslated natural language.
A consultant or contractor panel requires translation of the role heading, company type where meaningful, address geography, and contact-field labels; preserve proper names and contact values.
A legend requires one Chinese companion per visible legend entry. A single summary sentence never satisfies legend coverage.
Vertical and rotated labels are independent OCR tasks and must be rotated or normalized before semantic grouping.
Repeated FALL, FLOW, PITCH, ROOF, roof type, pipe notes, FROM ABOVE, room names, and equipment descriptions must be inventoried by exact visual location.
Multimodal inspection is authoritative for coverage. OCR absence never exempts visible embedded microtext.

Use overlapping high-resolution tiles and zoom every suspected microtext crop until the smallest glyphs are at least 12 rendered pixels high; labels smaller than FLOW in ordinary page view remain mandatory.
Bind each word to its local engineering symbol: FLOW/FALL arrows, slope arrows, degree values, FROM/TO relations, and leader direction are part of the same semantic block.

Only pure identifiers or values are literal-only. If an equipment code, drawing code, or dimension is accompanied by a natural-language descriptor, translate the descriptor and preserve the literal token.

Dense drawing indexes are never released as inline bilingual pages; on the original source page, precisely replace row text with black Chinese while preserving the table grid and identifiers. Historical source/translated pairs are evidence only.
placement_rules: Keep Chinese near the source. Score nearby right, left, above, below and local whitespace as whole-group candidates; do not use a fixed direction priority.
Use a short direct leader when the target is not immediately adjacent.
Small overlap with source text, table lines, hatching, or minor CAD geometry is acceptable when it preserves complete nearby translation.
Never omit a translation merely to avoid overlap.
Place every drawing-body Chinese companion in the immediate local visual group of its source. It may sit right, left, above, below, or at a slight angle, but may not fully cover the source.
For FLOW, FALL and slope labels, retain the arrow or direction relation in the Chinese companion; translating the word alone is incomplete.
Translation-to-translation overlap and clipped Chinese are release-blocking.
Shrink and wrap locally before moving far away.
For consultant panels and title blocks, translate inside the same semantic panel or cell whenever possible.

For company contact panels, preserve panel borders and logos, clear only confirmed ordinary text glyphs, then re-typeset source plus Chinese in black. State-bearing metadata keeps the source and uses nearby blue Chinese; pure prose/index metadata may use hierarchy-preserving black bilingual reflow.
For drawing-index title cells, preserve row number, drawing/model number, size and all grid lines; re-typeset source plus Chinese inside the title cell in one final PDF.

In drawing indexes, a newly visible item number is a hard semantic boundary. One item may span multiple physical subrows and drawing numbers, but neither source nor Chinese may cross into the next numbered item.

When an item number repeats with a different drawing or model number, treat each (item number, drawing/model number, ruled row range) as an independent semantic block even when the prose appears continuous.
